claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I have a few questions:

1. First, how old is Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 16, I need to ask a follow-up question:

Is Alex currently in full-time education (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or similar), or enrolled on an approved training course? Or has Alex left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has recently left education. He's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to clarify a bit further:

When you say Alex has signed up with the local careers service, is this an official government-approved training programme or careers service (such as one provided by the Careers Service in Northern Ireland or a similar government body), or is it more of an informal advisory service to help him explore options?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's the official careers service - you know, the one run by the local authority to help young people figure out their next steps after leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful to know.

I have a couple more questions about Alex's situation:

1. Has Alex registered with this official careers service within the last 20 weeks (roughly 5 months) since leaving education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - it's been fairly recent, within the last few months since he left school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more important question: Is Alex currently employed? Specifically, is he working more than 24 hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now. He's just taking his time to figure out what direction he wants to go in.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the picture:

Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care, and does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

And finally, can I just check: are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- **Alex is 16 years old** – Child Benefit can continue for children up to age 20 in certain circumstances
- **He has registered with an official careers service** – This is a qualifying body under Child Benefit rules
- **He registered recently (within 20 weeks of leaving education)** – This meets the time requirement
- **He is not working** – He's not employed for more than 24 hours per week
- **You are responsible for Alex and he lives with you** – This meets the care requirement
- **You live in the UK** – This meets the residency requirement

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. Please note that if Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he starts working more than 24 hours per week, or starts a job, apprenticeship, or returns to education), you would need to update HMRC as this could affect your eligibility.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old and has left full-time education. However, he has registered with an official local authority careers service (a qualifying body) within 20 weeks of leaving education. He is not currently employed (working fewer than 24 hours per week). Under Child Benefit rules, a child aged 16-17 who has left education can still qualify if they are registered with an approved careers service or similar body and are not in full-time paid work of more than 24 hours per week. Alex meets these conditions. Additionally, Alex lives with the claimant, who is responsible for his care, and the claimant resides in the UK. Therefore, the claimant is eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Although Alex is 16 and has left education, he qualifies for Child Benefit because he has recently registered with an official careers service (within 20 weeks of leaving education) and is not working. This meets the criteria for continuing Child Benefit eligibility for a 16-17 year old who has left education but is registered with an approved body.
